title: Cutting Ribbons
summary: Given an integer array ribbons where each element represents the length of a ribbon, and an integer k, determine the maximum length x such that you can cut at least k ribbons, each of length x.
statement: Given an integer array ribbons where each element represents the length of a ribbon, and an integer k, determine the maximum length x such that you can cut at least k ribbons, each of length x. You can cut any ribbon into any number of segments of positive integer lengths, or choose not to cut it at all. If it is impossible to achieve this, return 0.
constraints: There are at most 100000 ribbons, each with positive integer length.
Cut at least k equal integer-length pieces; return zero when even length one is impossible.
hints: For a proposed length x, ribbon r produces floor(r/x) pieces.
The total piece count never increases as x grows, so feasibility is monotonic.
Use an upper-mid binary search and keep feasible lengths on the left boundary.
The invariant retains every possible optimum, and termination at the largest feasible boundary returns exactly the requested maximum.
editorial: The invariant retains every possible optimum, and termination at the largest feasible boundary returns exactly the requested maximum.

tests.explanation: Length five yields one piece from each ribbon, while length six yields only two pieces.
Length four yields four pieces total, and length five yields only three.
